text.p: Following is a summary of opinions on Malaysia's inflation figures for December 1996.

The inflation rate as measured by the Consumer Price Index increased by 3.5 percent year-on-year last year against 3.4 percent in 1995, the Statistics Department said on Thursday. The CPI for December rose by 3.3 percent, year-on-year, from November.

PATRICK TAN, ECONOMIST AT BROKERS H.G. ASIA KUALA LUMPUR - "There are no great surprises. They are prety much as we expected. The numbers are quite respectable and are unlikely to fuel sentiments either way. We had forecast a rate of 3.6 percent for 1996. For 1997, our forecast is 3.8 percent."

CHUNG TIN FAH, HEAD OF RESEARCH AT OSK & PARTNERS - A very good number. We were expecting the CPI to be higher but we were wrong. I think the tight monetary policy and liberalisation of import duties helped contain inflation. Slower economic growth coupled with the strenghtening of ringgit should keep inflation below four percent this year.
FIONA LEONG, HEAD OF RESEARCH AT J.M. SASSOON, KUALA LUMPUR - There are no surpises in the figures. We did not expect there to be any.
